entities.name: Equisetum arvense
observations: Common horsetail extract was investigated for direct immunomodulatory effects on human lymphocytes in vitro.

entities.name: PMID:25088216
observations: 2014 study reported dose-dependent inhibition of activated human T-lymphocyte proliferation by standardized Equisetum arvense extract, with lower activation markers and intracellular IL-2; no apoptosis/necrosis was detected.

entities.name: PMID:29202511
observations: 2018 in-vitro study found horsetail preparations suppressed human lymphocyte activation/proliferation through IL-2-related effects; silica and isoquercitrin contributed, and IFN-gamma polyfunctionality was reduced.

entities.name: Horsetail suppresses lymphocytes
observations: In vitro, standardized Equisetum arvense extract dose-dependently reduced activated human T-cell proliferation and activation markers; apoptosis or necrosis was not detected (PMID:25088216).
In vitro horsetail preparations reduced human lymphocyte activation/proliferation via IL-2-related mechanisms; silica and isoquercitrin contributed (PMID:29202511).
